chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Yunus ibn Ya'qub has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub Al-Bajali.

key_terms.الْحَكَمُ بْنُ مِسْكِينٍ: Al-Hakam ibn Miskin, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key link in the chain
key_terms.يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ: Yunus ibn Ya'qub, a prominent narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the narration from Yun ibn Ya'qub transmitted in this book?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this statement to authenticate the specific isnad of Yunus ibn Ya'qub, a key narrator in Shia hadith literature, by tracing the chain back through his father (Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Hasan) and other reliable transmitters. This serves as a scholarly endorsement of Yunus's reliability (thiqa) and clarifies the transmission lineage for readers verifying the authenticity of the narrations in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih.
